business_problem: Lion Parcel needed to eliminate manual delivery-order transcription in finance, reduce document-entry errors, centralize document traceability, and convert growing volumes of paper logistics records into structured digital data for downstream financial reporting.
solution_summary: Lion Parcel implemented an OCR-driven document-processing pipeline on Alibaba Cloud to automate Finance handling of Delivery Orders. A client application sends parcel-label and delivery-order images to Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, where Qwen-VL-Plus Model extracts printed and handwritten content and returns structured JSON fields. That output is then passed into a backend processing layer that validates, normalizes, deduplicates, and applies business rules before storing the result in a database and making it available to downstream Finance workflows. The design intentionally blends automation with human validation so staff can review uncertain fields while still eliminating most repetitive data-entry work. Because the company operates at logistics scale—covering 99% of Indonesia and more than 50 countries with thousands of couriers and fleets—the shift from spreadsheets and hardcopy files to AI-assisted extraction gives Lion Parcel a more scalable, traceable, and accurate finance-document process.
business_outcome: Lion Parcel accelerated Delivery Order processing, improved finance-data accuracy, and created a centralized digital repository for a previously manual workflow.
architecture_clues: The OCR pipeline supports both printed and handwritten content
Backend processing validates and normalizes extracted fields before storage
The workflow includes user validation and duplicate detection
Results are exported into standardized finance-reporting formats
